author: hyunback
title: iGPU func tests fail en masse - no supported GPU devices found on runner
signature: Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed: [GPU] Can't get <PROPERTY> property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: iGPU Tests (func) / GPU
failed_jobs.symptom: 32927/43254 GPU func tests failed immediately with 'no supported devices found' (clinfo reports 0 platforms)

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status check failed because the iGPU Tests job failed

key_errors:
C++ exception with description "Exception from src/inference/src/cpp/core.cpp:272:
Exception from src/inference/src/dev/plugin.cpp:112:
Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed at src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/plugin.cpp:593:
[GPU] Can't get DEVICE_TYPE property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query.
[GPU] Please check OpenVINO documentation for GPU drivers setup guide." thrown in the test body.
root_cause: The 'Run clinfo' step on the iGPU self-hosted runner reported 'Number of platforms 0' before any OpenVINO test executed, meaning the OpenCL/Level-Zero GPU driver stack inside the test container could not enumerate the Intel iGPU render device (/dev/dri/renderD128 was passed to the container, but no OpenCL platform was exposed). Every GPU plugin test that queries a device property (DEVICE_TYPE, PERFORMANCE_HINT, OPTIMIZATION_CAPABILITIES, etc.) then hits the '!m_device_map.empty()' assertion in src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/plugin.cpp:593 and fails uniformly (32927 of 43254 tests), which is the signature of a runner/driver-level device-enumeration failure rather than a product regression introduced by the triggering commit (a GPU binary_mul_inplace kernel change, PR #38615/#637, unrelated to device enumeration).
reproduction_steps: N/A (requires the specific self-hosted iGPU runner/container image openvinogithubactions.azurecr.io/ov_test/ubuntu_22_04_x64_igpu:pr-37085); cannot be reproduced without access to that runner's GPU driver stack. To check driver health on the runner: run 'clinfo' inside the test container and confirm 'Number of platforms' > 0, then run any single GPU smoke test (e.g. --gtest_filter=TensorTest.smoke_dynamicOutputCallerOwnedUsmHostRebindsAllocation) against ov_gpu_func_tests.
recommended_actions: Check the self-hosted iGPU runner's host and container for GPU driver/firmware health (Intel Compute Runtime / NEO, Level-Zero, i915 kernel driver) - 'clinfo' reporting 0 platforms indicates the OpenCL ICD stack is broken or the device node is not accessible.
Verify /dev/dri/renderD128 is present and has correct permissions/group mappings (--group-add 44 --group-add 993) on the runner host at the time of this run.
Restart or re-provision the affected iGPU runner if the driver stack is confirmed broken; check for a recent host OS/driver update or container image change coinciding with this failure.

Add a pre-flight health check step (clinfo/device enumeration) that fails fast with a clear infra error before running the full ~43k test GPU suite, to avoid wasting ~40 minutes of CI time on a doomed run.
prevention_strategies: Add a lightweight GPU-device-availability smoke check as the very first step of the iGPU test job (fail fast with a clear 'runner GPU unavailable' message) instead of letting all 43k tests run and fail individually. Monitor self-hosted iGPU runner fleet health (driver versions, device node permissions) with periodic health checks independent of CI runs.
historical_context: No prior post-commit investigation in this database recorded the same '!m_device_map.empty()' / 'no supported devices found' signature. A related but distinct iGPU infrastructure issue (HuggingFace Hub 429 rate limit during LLM accuracy tests, 2026-10-12) and a GitHub 504 cloning openvino.genai.git (2026-10-19) were previously recorded for the GPU test lanes, both being transient external-service/network issues rather than device-enumeration failures.
